name: vindication
description: Relief from negative social pressure such as accusation, suspicion, or doubt.
alternateDefinitions: Christians refer to vindication as God's judgment of those who have done the right thing.
perceptions: You or someone close achieved an important outcome.
Others were skeptical you could do it.
examples: Winning the event despite doubt from others and perhaps yourself.
Being proven innocent after a false accusation.

comparisons.description: Vindication is a form of triumph specifically about being proven right after a period of social doubt.

commentaries.quote: Psychology keeps trying to vindicate human nature. History keeps undermining the effort.
Scripture is laced with stories of vindication. It’s core to God’s project of redeeming his creation.
O Lord, deliver me from this lust of always vindicating myself

I hate being told that I’m wrong about something especially when there isn’t a way to prove that I’m right. This happened to me just a couple of weeks ago and oh, how I wanted to defend myself and dig up every bit of evidence I could find to state my case; but there was no evidence. It was one person’s recollection of events against another’s.
Victory is a thousand times sweeter when you're the underdog.
